title: EXP-124 - Hello World Part 8 Phase 6a: Variable FX_CustomerID Bindings on EditCustID and StaticCustID, EditCount Initial Value 1, Menu Page Handlers with Primary Events and a Second FX_SignInBtn Handler on FX_CustomerPortal, with a Close/Reopen Readback
objective: Build the Designer part of Hello World Part 8 Phase 6 (12:16-16:54) on FX_CustomerPortal (User scope), except Enabled When: first the Customer ID variable bindings deferred from Part 7 (EXP-107, EXP-111): EditCustID and StaticCustID Binding Type Variable, variable FX_CustomerID (the tutorial's Customer ID, FX_-named like FX_Count and FX_Page); EditCount's FX_Count binding Initial Value 1; three Form event handlers FX_SignInBtn2, FX_HomeBtn and FX_CartBtn (Set Values FX_Page = 1, 2, 3) set as the Primary event of ButtonSignIn, ButtonHome and ButtonCart; and a second handler on the existing event FX_SignInBtn (Set Values FX_Page = 2) after its Collection Refresh handler. T1 gate; T2 to T8 one change group each; T9 close/reopen readback and final audit. Enabled When on the menu buttons and the runtime check follow in EXP-125. Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Before browser interaction read AGENTS.md (the repository file, at the start of every task), docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt8.md Phase 6 (lines 170-186) and transcript lines 433-473 (12:16-16:54), recipes/session/session-expiry-and-stale-designer.md, and only the final Outcome (operator) sections of the EXP-123, EXP-120, EXP-117, EXP-111, EXP-107, EXP-056 and EXP-055 records. Read nothing else: no other records and no later Part 8 phases. In a continuation task, AGENTS.md and the current task's part of this record are enough.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-124-hello-world-part-8-phase-6a-customer-id-binding-page-handlers.md and evidence/EXP-124/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.

Use the existing authenticated session without refresh, restart or configuration change. If a session expiry, logout card or sign-in page appears, record it and stop for the operator (EXP-107: the operator signs in manually); do not navigate, type credentials or screenshot a filled sign-in form. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection. Answer any prompt within the same task; never leave a prompt, dialog, menu or unsaved change open across tasks. After any pause, inspect the state read-only before acting and never replay an earlier action. Signed-out session (EXP-116): a server-event error together with a portal tab reading 'Logout Successful' means the session ended; record it and stop for the operator.

Task boundary: do only what the current task instruction lists and stop at its end, even when later steps of this brief remain; report the next step instead of performing it. Turn budget (EXP-109, EXP-111): if a task cannot finish, stop only at a step boundary right after a Save (never with an unsaved change, open list, editor or dialog) and report the next step.

Server-event rule (EXP-103-R2 lesson): if any action raises 'The server event processing returned an error', answer OK once, record it and stop blocked for an operator Designer reload; never try another route, retry, close or reopen after that error. Console-error stop (EXP-110-R2 lesson: a Caption commit can fail silently with HTTP 400 and surface only at the next server event): record the page console error count shown in the browser tool output at the start of each task and after every action in T1 to T9; if it rises after any action, record the action and the counts and stop blocked before any further click (no ellipsis, no Save, no close), leaving the state for the operator. Never read or inspect the console messages themselves. A rise can also come from a client-side Designer script error (EXP-111 T5: an uncaught TypeError at a component selection); the stop rule is the same, and the operator diagnoses the cause from the tool-written console log. A Caption commit that leaves Save disabled is also a stop signal (EXP-110-R2): record it and stop blocked before any further click.

Editing scope: stay in User scope throughout. If an 'Identify Your Editing Scope' dialog appears, confirm it shows User for the signed-in user and accept it unchanged; if it shows any other scope, Cancel it and stop blocked.

Designer gate (T1, read-only except at most one Form open): User scope; FX_CustomerPortal open and clean (Save disabled), no dialog open; if another Form tab is active, select FX_CustomerPortal's tab; if it is not open, open it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry (never Select Form OK). Record: Details > Event Handlers (every group and row; expected StdFormPredisplay with Set Values SETVARVALUES(FX_Page=1) and FX_SignInBtn with one Collection Refresh row; if a handler named FX_SignInBtn2, FX_HomeBtn or FX_CartBtn exists, or FX_SignInBtn has more than one row, record it and stop blocked); Details > Variables (expected FX_Count and FX_Page under Form - Temporary and fds_SC2 under Form - Persistent; record whether FX_CustomerID exists and where; its presence is not a stop). Then select each of these by its Components row Type cell, confirm the Properties header names it, and record the named rows (expanding groups is view only; open no ellipsis or list): EditCustID (FlexLayoutMain > Region02: signinpage; Binding Type and Binding, expected None and blank); StaticCustID (FlexLayoutHeader > Region01: user; Binding Type and Binding, expected None and blank); EditCount (Binding Type Variable, Binding variables.FX_Count); ButtonSignIn, ButtonHome and ButtonCart (FlexLayoutMain > Region00: menu; Events > Primary, expected blank; if any is not blank, record it and stop blocked); ButtonSignIn2 (Events > Primary, expected FX_SignInBtn). If EditCustID or StaticCustID already has Binding Type Variable, record it and stop blocked. Verify Save is still disabled. Record the baseline console error count. Screenshots: the Event Handlers tab; the Variables tab; ButtonSignIn's Events group.

Efficiency rules (operator, 2026-10-16): screenshots only for the decisive states named in this brief; do not re-open saved images unless a decision needs it; one untargeted snapshot per step; read only the named sources; never search or read the worker's own session transcript. Use inline untargeted snapshots; never save snapshots to files and Grep them (EXP-109 ran out of turns that way). Lists (EXP-111 lesson): choose a list option by clicking it; never pick options with arrow keys, Enter or Tab while a list is open, because Tab commits the highlighted item. Stale references (operator ruling, EXP-111): the allowance is one fresh untargeted snapshot per 'Ref not found' error, not one per task. Snapshot size (EXP-114): if an untargeted snapshot is too large to return inline, take targeted snapshots of the needed panel instead (record that); never save snapshots to files.

Property rules (EXP-055, EXP-056, EXP-111, EXP-120): select a component by its Components row (click its Type cell) and confirm the Properties header names it. Lists: open the list with its arrow and click the planned option, then leave the field by clicking a neutral row (never Tab or arrow keys while a list is open); if the planned option is absent, close the list without choosing and stop blocked before any OK or Save. Text fields: click the value cell, one plain fill, one Tab; verify. At most one correction per field. Record the console error count after each action. After each performed step exactly one Designer Save, recording its response and the Save state. Answer an OK-only informational prompt with OK and record it verbatim; any other prompt not covered here: record it, choose the non-changing answer (No or Cancel) and stop blocked. Close every nested dialog you opened with its OK (planned change) or Cancel (no change), innermost first; never leave one open across tasks.

Customer ID variable binding (T2 EditCustID; T3 StaticCustID; one component per task; EXP-120 route): select the component; Binding Type list: click Variable (record the options; if Variable is absent, close the list and stop blocked). Click the Binding ellipsis once and record the dialog (expected 'Edit Variable Binding': Variable combobox, Initial Value, Clear On Refresh?, Refresh Value) with a screenshot before any entry; if it differs or asks for anything else, Cancel and stop blocked before the Save. Click the Variable combobox once and type FX_CustomerID key by key (click an FX_CustomerID list entry only if one with exactly that name is offered; never pick another variable); leave Initial Value blank, Clear On Refresh unchecked and Refresh Value untouched; OK once. Verify Binding Type Variable and Binding variables.FX_CustomerID (record the exact text), then one Designer Save. Screenshots per task: the dialog before the entry; the dialog with FX_CustomerID before OK; the Binding rows before the Save; the Save response state.

EditCount initial value (T4): select EditCount; click its Binding ellipsis once and record the Edit Variable Binding dialog as it opens; it must show Variable FX_Count (otherwise Cancel and stop blocked). Click the Initial Value field, one plain fill 1, one Tab; verify; leave every other field unchanged; OK once. Verify Binding Type Variable and Binding variables.FX_Count are unchanged, then one Designer Save. Screenshots: the dialog at open; the dialog with Initial Value 1 before OK; the Save response state.

Menu page handler and Primary event (T5 FX_SignInBtn2 = 1 on ButtonSignIn; T6 FX_HomeBtn = 2 on ButtonHome; T7 FX_CartBtn = 3 on ButtonCart; one handler and one button per task; EXP-117 and EXP-123 routes; each handler is created with New, never with the handler Copy button). Step A: Details > Event Handlers > New (+) once; in the Event Handler dialog type the task's handler name key by key and confirm with OK (record the dialog first); record the new group and row. Select the row; Response Type list: click Set Values. Open the Parameters ellipsis once; open the Variables ellipsis once (an 'Edit Set Variable Values' list, expected empty); New once ('Edit Set Variable Value Pair'); type FX_Page into the Target combobox key by key and commit with Tab (or click an FX_Page entry if offered; never another variable); fill Value N and Tab; verify both; OK on the pair dialog, then OK on each enclosing dialog. Verify the handler row reads Response Type Set Values and Parameters SETVARVALUES(FX_Page=N) (record the exact text). One Designer Save. Step B: select the task's menu button by its Components row; in Events, open the Primary list and click the task's handler (the Form's own handlers are listed first, EXP-117; if absent, close the list and stop blocked); leave the field by clicking a neutral row; verify Primary; one Designer Save. Screenshots per task: the Event Handler dialog with the name; the pair dialog before OK; the handler row before the Save; the button's Events group before the Save; each Save response state.

Second FX_SignInBtn handler (T8): Details > Event Handlers > New (+) once; in the Event Handler dialog type FX_SignInBtn key by key, or click the existing FX_SignInBtn entry if the field offers it (record which); OK once. Expected: a second row in the FX_SignInBtn group, after the existing Collection Refresh row (record both rows with their sequence numbers). If a prompt about an existing name appears, record it verbatim and answer with the non-changing choice; if the dialog refuses the name, or the new row replaces, alters or reorders the Collection Refresh row, or lands in a different group, record it and stop blocked before any further change or Save (the operator decides). Then, on the new row only: Response Type Set Values; Parameters and Variables ellipses; New pair Target FX_Page (as in T5), Value 2; OK on each dialog. Verify the new row reads Set Values SETVARVALUES(FX_Page=2) and the first row still reads Collection Refresh with summary object2; ButtonSignIn2's Primary stays FX_SignInBtn (not touched). One Designer Save. Screenshots: the Event Handler dialog with the name; the pair dialog before OK; the FX_SignInBtn group with both rows before the Save; the Save response state.

Readback and audit (T9, one task): close the clean FX_CustomerPortal once through its Form-tab control (answer No to any save prompt, record its text), reopen it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry, and read: Details > Event Handlers (every group and row: StdFormPredisplay unchanged; FX_SignInBtn with Collection Refresh then Set Values SETVARVALUES(FX_Page=2); FX_SignInBtn2, FX_HomeBtn, FX_CartBtn with SETVARVALUES(FX_Page=1/2/3)); Details > Variables (FX_CustomerID and its category; FX_Count, FX_Page); EditCustID and StaticCustID Binding Type and Binding; EditCount Binding, with its Binding ellipsis opened once read-only to read Initial Value 1, then Cancel; the Primary of ButtonSignIn, ButtonHome, ButtonCart and ButtonSignIn2. Open no other dialog or list. Leave FX_CustomerPortal open and clean. Then, in the same task, write the documentation-only final audit into the record: decisive evidence for each acceptance check, the cumulative action audit with exact counts, the worker-written-file inventory, the cleanup inventory and the final state. Screenshots: Event Handlers; Variables; EditCustID's Binding rows; StaticCustID's Binding rows; the EditCount dialog; ButtonCart's Events group.

Before every click, use references from the most recent snapshot taken in the current task (not from find output); after any timeout or 'Ref not found', take one fresh untargeted snapshot and use only its references (one per error). ExtJS comboboxes are not <select> elements (EXP-101): open their list and click the option. Coordinates are allowed only once per field for a list arrow that has no reference (EXP-111: a value-cell double-click may expose it first); record each such click. Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection; never leave a prompt, list, editor or dialog open across tasks. Classify findings as observed only.

initial_instruction: T1 - Read-only gate for EXP-124. First read the repository file AGENTS.md, then hello-world-pt8.md lines 170-186 and transcript lines 433-473, recipes/session/session-expiry-and-stale-designer.md, and only the Outcome (operator) sections of EXP-123, EXP-120, EXP-117, EXP-111, EXP-107, EXP-056 and EXP-055, all before any browser action; read nothing else. Without shell/git access, record the starting state concisely. List the browser tabs before selecting one; identify the Web Client and Web Designer tabs. If either shows a session expiry, logout card, 'Logout Successful' or sign-in, record it and stop for the operator (do not sign in; never screenshot a filled sign-in form). Record the page console error count shown in the tool output (do not read the messages); if it rises after any action, record the action and stop. In the Designer confirm User scope, that FX_CustomerPortal is open and clean (select its Form tab if another is active; open it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry only if it is not open) and that no dialog is open. If any action raises the server-event error, answer OK once, record it and stop. Record Details > Event Handlers (StdFormPredisplay and FX_SignInBtn with one Collection Refresh row expected; no FX_SignInBtn2, FX_HomeBtn or FX_CartBtn) and Details > Variables (record whether FX_CustomerID exists). Select by Components row Type cell and record: EditCustID and StaticCustID Binding Type and Binding (None and blank expected); EditCount Binding (variables.FX_Count); ButtonSignIn, ButtonHome, ButtonCart Events > Primary (blank expected); ButtonSignIn2 Events > Primary (FX_SignInBtn expected). Open no ellipsis or list; verify Save is still disabled. Screenshots: Event Handlers; Variables; ButtonSignIn's Events group. Use inline snapshots only (targeted panel snapshots if an untargeted one is too large). Make no change in T1. This is the end of T1 even though later brief steps remain. Create the EXP-124 record with the gate, the readings, the action audit and the file inventory, with screenshots under evidence/EXP-124/ (distinct filenames), and stop with no dialog open.
notes: Part 8 Phase 6a after EXP-123 (Phase 5 accepted 2026-10-20), drafted by the operator assistant from the EXP-123 brief with the Edit Variable Binding route of EXP-120, the handler and Primary routes of EXP-117 and the Set Values pair route of EXP-123. Phase 6 is split for the 12-task limit: 6a here (Designer bindings, handlers, Primary events), 6b in EXP-125 (Enabled When FX_CustomerID not blank on the three menu buttons, then the runtime check). Tutorial mapping: Customer ID -> FX_CustomerID (FX_ naming as FX_Count and FX_Page; the Variable binding of EditCustID and StaticCustID was narrated in Part 7 but deferred by the operator, EXP-107 and EXP-111, because the variable did not exist; 6b's Enabled When needs it); Sign In Btn2 / Home Btn / Cart Btn -> FX_SignInBtn2 / FX_HomeBtn / FX_CartBtn; Page -> FX_Page; Count -> FX_Count. Deviations from the tutorial: it copies the first handler with the Copy button and renames it; this brief creates each with New. It adds the second FX_SignInBtn handler from ButtonSignIn2's Primary-event ellipsis; this brief uses Details > Event Handlers > New with the existing event name, and stops for the operator if that does not append a row. Planned tasks: T1 gate; T2 EditCustID, T3 StaticCustID, T4 EditCount (1 Save each); T5 ButtonSignIn, T6 ButtonHome, T7 ButtonCart (handler then Primary, 2 Saves each); T8 second FX_SignInBtn handler (1 Save); T9 close/reopen readback and final audit. Ten Saves in all. exact_values: FX_CustomerID, FX_SignInBtn2, FX_SignInBtn, FX_HomeBtn, FX_CartBtn, FX_Page. deny_browser_javascript. Approval pending from the operator.
